If $AB=25$, $BC=14$, and $GF=7$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Connect OE, let OG intersect EF at point H, and draw AP$\perp$BC at point P, intersecting OE at point Q, as shown in the figure.\\
$\because$AB=AC, AP$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ $BP=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore$ $AP=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BP^{2}}=\sqrt{25^{2}-7^{2}}=24.$\\
$\because$Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$OA=OC.\\
$\because$EA=EB,\\
$\therefore$OE is the median line of $\triangle ABC$.\\
$\therefore$OE$\parallel$BC and $OE=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle ABC,$ $\angle AOE=\angle ACB.$\\
$\because AB=AC,$\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ACB.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle AOE.$\\
$\therefore AO=AE.$ That is, $\triangle AEO$ is an isosceles triangle.\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AQE=$\angle$APB=90$^\circ$.\\
$\therefore$AP$\perp$OE at point Q.\\
$\therefore EQ=OQ=\frac{1}{2}OE=\frac{7}{2}.$\\
$\therefore$ $AQ=\sqrt{AE^{2}-EQ^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{25}{2}\right)^{2}-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^{2}}=12.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AEO}=\frac{1}{2}OE\cdot AQ=\frac{1}{2}\times 7\times 12=42.$\\
Connect EG, OF,\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$GF, OE=GF=7,\\
$\therefore$Quadrilateral OEGF is a parallelogram.\\
$\therefore$HE=HF, HO=HG.\\
$\because$PQ=AP−AQ=24−12=12,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{parallelogram} OEGF}=GF\cdot PQ=7\times 12=84.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle OEH}={S}_{\triangle GFH}=\frac{1}{4}{S}_{\text{parallelogram} OEGF}=\frac{1}{4}\times 84=21.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{shaded}}={S}_{\triangle AEO}+{S}_{\triangle OEH}+{S}_{\triangle GFH}=42+21+21=\boxed{84}.$

Segments $OG$ and $EF$ are drawn. If $AB=25$, $BC=14$, and $GF=7$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution}: Connect OE, let OG intersect EF at point H, and draw AP$\perp$BC at point P, intersecting OE at point Q, as shown in the figure.\\
$\because$AB=AC, AP$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ $BP=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore$ $AP=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BP^{2}}=\sqrt{25^{2}-7^{2}}=24.$\\
$\because$Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$OA=OC.\\
$\because$EA=EB,\\
$\therefore$OE is the median line of $\triangle ABC$.\\
$\therefore$OE$\parallel$BC and $OE=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle ABC,$ $\angle AOE=\angle ACB.$\\
$\because AB=AC,$\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ACB.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle AOE.$\\
$\therefore AO=AE.$ That is, $\triangle AEO$ is an isosceles triangle.\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AQE=$\angle$APB=90$^\circ$.\\
$\therefore$AP$\perp$OE at point Q.\\
$\therefore EQ=OQ=\frac{1}{2}OE=\frac{7}{2}.$\\
$\therefore$ $AQ=\sqrt{AE^{2}-EQ^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{25}{2}\right)^{2}-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^{2}}=12.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AEO}=\frac{1}{2}OE\cdot AQ=\frac{1}{2}\times 7\times 12=42.$\\
Connect EG, OF,\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$GF, OE=GF=7,\\
$\therefore$Quadrilateral OEGF is a parallelogram.\\
$\therefore$HE=HF, HO=HG.\\
$\because$PQ=AP-AQ=24-12=12,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{parallelogram}\ OEGF}=GF\cdot PQ=7\times 12=84.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle OEH}={S}_{\triangle GFH}=\frac{1}{4}{S}_{\text{parallelogram}\ OEGF}=\frac{1}{4}\times 84=21.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{shaded}}={S}_{\triangle AEO}+{S}_{\triangle OEH}+{S}_{\triangle GFH}=42+21+21=\boxed{84}.$

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the parallelogram $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, $AC=AB$, $E$ is the midpoint of side $AB$, and $G$ and $F$ are points on side $BC$. Segments $OG$ and $EF$ are drawn. If $AB=25$, $BC=14$, and $GF=7$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution}: Connect OE, let OG intersect EF at point H, and draw AP$\perp$BC at point P, intersecting OE at point Q, as shown in the figure.\\
$\because$AB=AC, AP$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ $BP=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore$ $AP=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BP^{2}}=\sqrt{25^{2}-7^{2}}=24.$\\
$\because$Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$OA=OC.\\
$\because$EA=EB,\\
$\therefore$OE is the median line of $\triangle ABC$.\\
$\therefore$OE$\parallel$BC and $OE=\frac{1}{2}BC=7.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle ABC,$ $\angle AOE=\angle ACB.$\\
$\because AB=AC,$\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ACB.$\\
$\therefore \angle AEO=\angle AOE.$\\
$\therefore AO=AE.$ That is, $\triangle AEO$ is an isosceles triangle.\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AQE=$\angle$APB=90$^\circ$.\\
$\therefore$AP$\perp$OE at point Q.\\
$\therefore EQ=OQ=\frac{1}{2}OE=\frac{7}{2}.$\\
$\therefore$ $AQ=\sqrt{AE^{2}-EQ^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{25}{2}\right)^{2}-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^{2}}=12.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AEO}=\frac{1}{2}OE\cdot AQ=\frac{1}{2}\times 7\times 12=42.$\\
Connect EG, OF,\\
$\because$OE$\parallel$GF, OE=GF=7,\\
$\therefore$Quadrilateral OEGF is a parallelogram.\\
$\therefore$HE=HF, HO=HG.\\
$\because$PQ=AP-AQ=24-12=12,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{parallelogram}\ OEGF}=GF\cdot PQ=7\times 12=84.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle OEH}={S}_{\triangle GFH}=\frac{1}{4}{S}_{\text{parallelogram}\ OEGF}=\frac{1}{4}\times 84=21.$\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\text{shaded}}={S}_{\triangle AEO}+{S}_{\triangle OEH}+{S}_{\triangle GFH}=42+21+21=\boxed{84}.$

Image description: The outer frame in the figure is parallelogram ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. E is on side AB, G and F are on the bottom side BC, and G is to the left of F. The figure draws OG and EF, and they intersect inside; the shaded part includes the upper triangle AEO, and the two opposite small triangles formed by the crossing of OG and EF in quadrilateral OEGF.

Reasoning: By the coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(14,0). Because AB=AC=25, A is on the perpendicular bisector of BC, that is, x=7; also AB=25, so the height of A is sqrt(25^2-7^2)=24, therefore A=(7,24). E is the midpoint of AB, so E=((7+0)/2,(24+0)/2)=(3.5,12). The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of AC, O=((7+14)/2,(24+0)/2)=(10.5,12). Therefore EO=10.5-3.5=7, and EO is horizontal.

The base EO of triangle AEO is 7, and the height is 24-12=12, so the area is (1/2)*7*12=42.

Let G=(t,0), F=(t+7,0), because GF=7 and is horizontal on BC. EO and GF are parallel and both have length 7, so quadrilateral OEGF is a parallelogram. Its base is 7, its height is 12, and its area is 7*12=84. Segments OG and EF are the two diagonals of this parallelogram; the diagonals divide the parallelogram into four small triangles of equal area; the shading in the figure takes two of the opposite triangles, so the total area of these two parts is 84/2=42.

Total shaded area = area of triangle AEO 42 + area of the two shaded triangles inside quadrilateral OEGF 42 = 84.
